theme: How to split an app: business logic, presentation logic and separation of concerns

terms.definition: The rules of your app that stay the same no matter how the screen looks.
terms.example: Keep the business logic out of the view controller.

terms.definition: A design idea where each part of the code has one clear job.
terms.example: Separation of concerns makes this module easy to read.

terms.definition: The code that decides how data looks on the screen, like text and format.
terms.example: The price format is presentation logic, so it goes in the view model.

video.description:
Learn to explain splitting an app into clear layers: Business Logic, Separation of Concerns & Presentation Logic, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Business Logic - The rules of your app that stay the same no matter how the screen looks.
Separation of Concerns - A design idea where each part of the code has one clear job.
Presentation Logic - The code that decides how data looks on the screen, like text and format.

Explain Business Logic, Separation of Concerns & Presentation Logic in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Business Logic, Separation of Concerns, Presentation Logic 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Business Logic - The rules of your app that stay the same no matter how the screen looks.
한국어: Business Logic: 화면 모양과 상관없이 늘 같은 앱의 규칙

Separation of Concerns - A design idea where each part of the code has one clear job.
한국어: Separation of Concerns: 코드의 각 부분이 하나의 명확한 역할만 갖게 하는 설계 원칙

Presentation Logic - The code that decides how data looks on the screen, like text and format.
한국어: Presentation Logic: 텍스트와 형식처럼 데이터가 화면에 어떻게 보일지 정하는 코드

landscape.hook: Can you explain Business Logic, Separation of Concerns and Presentation Logic in English?

dialogue.title: Mixing two jobs

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the checkout view controller adds the prices and also formats them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That mixes business logic with display code.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It is a rule of your app, like adding prices in `total`. It stays the same on every screen.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And the dollar sign in `label` is presentation logic?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Presentation logic decides how data looks, like `label` does.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So where should each one go?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Follow separation of concerns: each type has one clear job.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. Keep business logic in `total` and presentation logic in `label`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I see. Separation of concerns also makes tests easier, right?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, you test `total` without any screen.
Keep the business logic out of the view controller.
